title: ENDO-EVE Effectively detect endometriosis and provide coordinated, holistic treatment
summary: The quantitative evaluation refers to a heterogeneous and complex new form of care, which consists of two independent interventions within the overall project: Firstly, the evaluation of a new, structured referral strategy from the general practitioner to the respective endometriosis center (Intervention 1), and secondly, the evaluation of a digital companion program provided to patients by the endometriosis center in addition to therapy (Intervention 2), which is compared in an RCT against a control group under the currently usual care conditions.

interventions.name:
Control group - Questionnaires + Eve
Participants in the control group utilize exclusively the assessments defined in the study protocol at the designated measurement time points (T1–T8). Optionally, weekly baseline monitoring may be conducted, without daily inquiries being posed. Self-care content

Intervention Group 1 – Questionnaires + Eve
In addition to the scheduled assessments, participants gain access to low-threshold, pre-approved self-care content (texts, audio exercises; Low-Risk Whitelist). Weekly monitoring remains active; if defined thresholds are exceeded, a brief daily check may

Intervention Group 2 – Questionnaires + Eve + eCoaches
In this study arm, in addition to self-care content, coaching sessions (via video) and notifications to the care team ("light alerts") are available; these may be offered or mandatorily triggered if predefined thresholds are exceeded. Critical

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Statutory health insurance (GKV) with one of the participating health insurance companies
German skills: fluent
Smartphone
Typical symptoms of endometriosis such as cycle-related pain (e.g., dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia, dysuria, dyschezia, cyclic/acyclic pelvic pain, infertility) or imaging findings (ultrasound, MRI, etc.)
Exclusion criteria:
Not insured with participating health insurance companies
Over the age of 50
